testName: Class B Knowledge Test #1 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: When it is hard to see, such as at dawn or dusk, how can a driver make their vehicle more visible?

options.text: Flash their lights on and off.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on their headlights.
questions.explanation: Use your headlights on low beam when driving at dawn, dusk, or in bad weather. This helps other drivers see you.

questions.question: Who can get a hazardous materials endorsement?

options.text: A U.S. citizen or permanent resident.
Someone who completes their own background check.
Someone new to the United States.

questions.correctAnswerText: A U.S. citizen or permanent resident.
questions.explanation: You must be a U.S. citizen or lawful permanent resident to get a hazardous materials endorsement. If you give up your U.S. citizenship, you lose this endorsement.

questions.question: What should happen with dual tires?

options.text: They should always touch each other.
They should touch each other fairly often.
They should not touch each other.

questions.correctAnswerText: They should not touch each other.
questions.explanation: Dual tires must not touch each other or any other part of the vehicle. Check this when inspecting your vehicle.

questions.question: Is texting while driving safer or more dangerous than talking on a cell phone?
questions.correctAnswerText: More dangerous.
questions.explanation: Texting while driving is more dangerous than talking on a phone. It distracts your mind and takes your hands off the wheel.

questions.question: What should you do if you must drive through flowing water or a large puddle?
questions.correctAnswerText: Apply the brakes gently.
questions.explanation: Slow down, shift to a low gear, and apply the brakes gently. This keeps water and dirt out of your brake system.

questions.question: What is usually true about a distracted driver?

options.text: They usually follow the rules of the road.
They usually notice hazards more slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: They usually notice hazards more slowly.
questions.explanation: Distracted drivers are slower to see dangers on the road or may not see them at all.

questions.question: If there is a fire in a cargo trailer, should you open the trailer doors?

options.text: No, do not open the doors.
Cover the trailer with a heavy blanket.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, do not open the doors.
questions.explanation: Do not open trailer doors during a cargo fire. Opening the doors gives the fire more oxygen and makes it worse.

questions.question: What does an application pressure gauge show?

options.text: How much air pressure is being applied to the brakes right now.
How much air pressure is available.
How much air pressure is needed to stop the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: How much air pressure is being applied to the brakes right now.
questions.explanation: This gauge shows the air pressure currently being used on the brakes. It helps you see if your brakes are starting to wear out.

questions.question: How often should you stop to rest while driving on a long trip?
questions.correctAnswerText: Every two hours
questions.explanation: Stop to rest at least once every two hours or every 100 miles. This helps you stay alert and avoid fatigue.

questions.question: How much should you reduce your speed on packed snow?
questions.correctAnswerText: By one-half or more.
questions.explanation: Reduce your speed by half or more when driving on packed snow. Snow reduces how well your tires grip the road.

questions.question: How can you prevent your vehicle from rolling backward when you start to move?

options.text: Partly engage the clutch before lifting your foot off the brake pedal.
Place the vehicle in second gear.
Use the parking brake when stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Partly engage the clutch before lifting your foot off the brake pedal.
questions.explanation: To stop your vehicle from rolling backward when you start to move, partly engage the clutch before you lift your foot off the brake pedal.

questions.question: Brake linings should be:
questions.correctAnswerText: Free of oil.
questions.explanation: Brake linings must be free of oil and grease. They should not be loose or too thin.

questions.question: Truck tractors with air brakes made on or after March 1, 1997 must have:
questions.correctAnswerText: An Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS).
questions.explanation: Truck tractors with air brakes made on or after March 1, 1997 must have an anti-lock braking system.

questions.question: In cool weather, as the temperature rises and ice begins to melt, what happens to the road?

options.text: It is usually safe to drive.
The road becomes even more slippery.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road becomes even more slippery.
questions.explanation: As the temperature rises and ice melts, water sits on top of the ice, making the road even more slippery. Always slow down and drive carefully on slippery roads.

questions.question: What should you do if your vehicle gets stuck on railroad tracks?

options.text: Get out of the vehicle and call for help.
Keep trying to get your vehicle off the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get out of the vehicle and call for help.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle gets stuck on railroad tracks, leave the vehicle immediately and move away from the tracks. Find the emergency number on the signal box at the crossing and call 911 or the emergency number listed.

questions.question: What is the best advice for driving in fog?

options.text: Avoid driving in fog if possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid driving in fog if possible.
questions.explanation: Driving in fog is dangerous. Avoid it if you can. If you must drive in fog, use your low beam headlights and fog lights, even during the day.

questions.question: Eating while driving is:

options.text: A good way to save time.
Okay if the food is easy to eat.

questions.correctAnswerText: A dangerous activity.
questions.explanation: Eating, smoking, and drinking while driving are distracting and dangerous. Plan to stop and eat when taking a long trip.

questions.question: When driving a vehicle with an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS), you should:

options.text: Always pump the brakes several times before holding down the brake pedal.
Press the brake pedal as hard as possible every time you slow or stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake normally.
questions.explanation: Brake the same way in a vehicle with ABS as in a vehicle without ABS. ABS automatically works to prevent wheel lockup when you apply the brakes.

questions.question: During the driving test, what should you do when approaching a railroad crossing?

options.text: Pass another vehicle on the tracks if it is going too slow.
Get out of the vehicle to check for a train.
Do not change gears while your vehicle is on the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not change gears while your vehicle is on the tracks.
questions.explanation: During the driving test, do not stop, change gears, pass another vehicle, or change lanes while any part of your vehicle is on railroad tracks.

questions.question: Convex mirrors:

options.text: Cannot be used on vehicles carrying hazardous materials.
Help drivers see a larger area.

questions.correctAnswerText: Help drivers see a larger area.
questions.explanation: Convex mirrors on large vehicles allow drivers to see a wider area than flat mirrors. However, objects appear smaller and farther away than they really are.

questions.question: When taking the on-road driving skills test, what vehicle must you use?

options.text: You can use any vehicle type.
You must use the same type of vehicle you want to be licensed to drive.
The vehicle type does not matter.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must use the same type of vehicle you want to be licensed to drive.
questions.explanation: You must take the on-road test with the same type of vehicle you want a license to drive.

questions.question: What is reaction distance?

options.text: The distance you travel from when you decide to brake until you actually press the brake pedal.
The distance you travel from when a hazard first appears until you see it.
The distance you travel from when you see a hazard until you decide to brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: The distance you travel from when you decide to brake until you actually press the brake pedal.
questions.explanation: Reaction distance is how far your vehicle travels between the moment you decide to brake and when your foot actually hits the brake pedal.

questions.question: If you are convicted of a traffic violation while driving your personal car, what must you do?

options.text: Your CDL will not be affected.
Law enforcement will tell your employer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tell your employer.
questions.explanation: You must notify your employer within 30 days of any traffic violation conviction, regardless of what vehicle you were driving. Parking violations do not count.

questions.question: Which maneuver is part of the basic vehicle control skills test?
questions.correctAnswerText: Alley dock.
questions.explanation: The basic vehicle control skills test includes maneuvers like straight line backing, offset parking, parallel parking, and alley docking.

questions.question: When drivers turn, which direction do they usually look?

options.text: In the direction they are turning.
In the opposite direction of the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the direction they are turning.
questions.explanation: When turning, drivers look in the direction of the turn. Even without a signal, a driver's body movements can show they plan to turn.

questions.question: When are containerized loads used?

options.text: When cargo is too large for a truck.
When cargo has been or will be transported by train or ship.

questions.correctAnswerText: When cargo has been or will be transported by train or ship.
questions.explanation: Containerized loads are used when freight is carried partly by rail or ship. The driver must ensure containers do not exceed safe weight limits.

questions.question: What is the minimum acceptable tread depth for rear tires?
questions.correctAnswerText: 2/32 of an inch.
questions.explanation: Front tires must have at least 4/32 of an inch of tread. Other tires must have at least 2/32 of an inch of tread.

questions.question: If you feel tired and yawn a lot while driving, what should you do?

options.text: Pull over and take a nap.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over and take a nap.
questions.explanation: If you feel tired while driving, stop and sleep. Do not try to reach your destination while tired. Caffeine is not a safe substitute for rest.

questions.question: Before trying to put out an engine fire, what should you do first?

options.text: Press the accelerator to use up remaining fuel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn off the engine.
questions.explanation: Turn off the engine as soon as safely possible if there is an engine fire. Do not open the hood when trying to put out the fire.

questions.question: If your vehicle catches fire, which action should you avoid?

options.text: Park away from buildings, trees, brush, and other vehicles.
Call emergency services and tell them your location.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull into a service station.
questions.explanation: Leave the road and stop in an open area. Do not pull into a service station because the fuel there could catch fire. Report the fire and your location to emergency services.

questions.question: What type of brakes do most newer heavy-duty trucks use?
questions.correctAnswerText: Dual air brakes
questions.explanation: Most newer heavy-duty trucks use dual air brake systems. This system has two separate air brake systems that share one set of brake controls.

questions.question: How can a driver stay alert while driving?
questions.correctAnswerText: Stay fit and healthy
questions.explanation: Heavy foods and warm cabs can make you drowsy while driving. Exercise and a healthy diet will help you stay alert behind the wheel.

questions.question: Why are parked delivery trucks hazardous?

options.text: Drivers are often in a hurry when leaving the truck and may not check for other vehicles.
Packages often fall out of the trucks onto the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers are often in a hurry when leaving the truck and may not check for other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Parked delivery trucks are dangerous because the driver may pull into traffic quickly without checking, or may step out of the vehicle without looking for other traffic.

questions.question: When stopping, how should you use the brake pedal?
questions.correctAnswerText: Push down gradually.
questions.explanation: Push the brake pedal down gradually when stopping. This helps you maintain control of your vehicle.

questions.question: Which vehicle requires a CDL?
questions.correctAnswerText: A school bus
questions.explanation: Military vehicles, authorized emergency vehicles, farm equipment, and recreational vehicles do not require a CDL. A school bus does require a CDL.

questions.question: Why is backing toward the driver's side recommended when towing a trailer?

options.text: The driver will have the best view.
Power lines should be on the passenger's side.
Other drivers can help on the passenger's side.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver will have the best view.
questions.explanation: Back toward the left side (driver's side) when towing. This gives the driver the best possible view of the trailer.

questions.question: What happens when brakes are out of adjustment?
questions.correctAnswerText: Some brakes overwork and fail.
questions.explanation: Brakes that are out of adjustment will fade before properly adjusted brakes. Check brake adjustment frequently to prevent brake problems.

questions.question: When are people usually the least alert?
questions.correctAnswerText: Late at night
questions.explanation: Drivers are least alert at night, especially after midnight. Most crashes from tired driving happen at night.

questions.question: How should you hold the steering wheel?

options.text: With one hand while the other rests.
With both hands for a firm grip.
Release it if the vehicle hits a bump.

questions.correctAnswerText: With both hands for a firm grip.
questions.explanation: Hold the steering wheel firmly with both hands on opposite sides of the wheel.

questions.question: Where must placards be placed on a vehicle carrying hazardous cargo?

options.text: Only on the front of the vehicle.
On the front, rear, and both sides of the vehicle.
Only on the driver's side of the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: On the front, rear, and both sides of the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Placards must be placed on the front, rear, and both sides of any vehicle carrying hazardous cargo so they can be seen from any direction.

questions.question: When you look under your vehicle during a pre-trip inspection and see fresh oil, this is:
questions.correctAnswerText: A problem.
questions.explanation: Before a trip, check under your vehicle for fresh oil, coolant, grease, or fuel leaks. Finding any of these is a problem.

questions.question: Which one is NOT a reason to cover cargo?

options.text: To protect people from spilled cargo
To protect the cargo from weather
To protect the cargo from animals

questions.correctAnswerText: To protect the cargo from animals
questions.explanation: Cover your cargo to protect people if it spills and to protect the cargo from bad weather.

questions.question: When you meet an aggressive driver, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Ignore hand gestures.
questions.explanation: Get out of the aggressive driver's way if you can. Do not make eye contact, as this may upset them more. Ignore any hand gestures they make.

questions.question: You should test the low pressure warning light by:

options.text: Starting the engine and using the trailer hand brake.
Quickly pressing and releasing the brake pedal.
Removing wheel chocks and releasing the parking brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Quickly pressing and releasing the brake pedal.
questions.explanation: Your low pressure warning light is important. Let the system build pressure first. Then test the warning light by pressing and releasing the brake pedal quickly. This releases air, and the light should come on when pressure gets too low.

questions.question: If you are not sure if the road is becoming icy, a driver should:

options.text: Roll down the window and touch the side mirror to feel for ice.

questions.correctAnswerText: Roll down the window and touch the side mirror to feel for ice.
questions.explanation: If you think ice might be forming but are not sure, open your window and feel the front of the side mirror, the mirror support, or the antenna. If ice has formed on these, the road is likely icy too.

questions.question: If you start a left turn before reaching the center of an intersection, you may:

options.text: Hit another vehicle with your left side.
Expect other drivers to move out of your way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hit another vehicle with your left side.
questions.explanation: Wait until you reach the center of the intersection before turning left. If you turn too early, the left side of your vehicle may hit another vehicle.

questions.question: To use controlled braking, you should:

options.text: Apply your brakes hard without locking the wheels.

questions.correctAnswerText: Apply your brakes hard without locking the wheels.
questions.explanation: Controlled braking means applying the brakes as hard as possible without locking the wheels. Keep your steering wheel movements small when using this method.

questions.question: If you must drive in reverse using driver's side backing, this:

options.text: Is only good when it is raining.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is always a good idea.
questions.explanation: If you must back up, back toward the driver's side. This gives you the best view of where you are going.

questions.question: When it is hard to see and other drivers are near you, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Use low beam lights.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights when it is hard to see near other drivers, such as at dawn, dusk, or in bad weather. High beams can make it harder for other drivers to see.

questions.question: When turning, when should you turn off the turn signal?
questions.correctAnswerText: After the turn is done
questions.explanation: Keep your signal on the whole time you are turning. Do not turn it off until the turn is finished.
